captions: A [£250,000] flat | advertised at [6.5%] yield | earns closer to [4.1%] | once the *service charge,* | *ground rent,* | *management* | and one month's *void* | come off. That gap is the difference | between [GROSS YIELD] | and [NET YIELD,] | and it's the number that decides | whether a property *pays you* | or [COSTS YOU.] I'm Jake, | the founder of | [CALIBRE ACQUIRE.] I've worked in property | for [14 YEARS,] | and last year | we transacted on over | [£30 MILLION] | in property. I help investors | get out of *underperforming* property assets | and into property assets | that work [HARDER] | for them. If you've bought something | on the *advertised yield* | and the money landing in your account | is far less | than you expected, | this is [WHY.] We've sold buildings like | [FABIAN HOUSE] | on Cannon Street Road, | which has *nine flats* | and *two shops,* | at [£4,775,000.] On every sale like that, | the buyer priced the building | on what was left | after [COSTS,] | not on the figure | in the advert. In this video, | I'll cover the | [FIVE COSTS] | that come off every yield, | worked through a *leasehold flat* | and a *freehold building* | side by side, | show you the [TWO TRAPS] | that make advertised yields | look better than they are, | and explain how *finance* | changes the picture. If you're considering a property | and want to [STRESS TEST] it | within a few minutes, | I built a set of | *investment calculators* | you can use for [FREE.] Comment [SEND] | or use the link below. First, | the [DEFINITIONS.] Gross yield | is the *annual rent* | divided by the [PRICE.] Net yield | is the annual rent | minus the *running costs,* | divided by the [PRICE.] Gross yield | is your *salary before tax.* Net yield | is what [LANDS] | in your account. Now, | the [COSTS.] First, | there's the [SERVICE CHARGE.] On a leasehold flat, | it's often the | *biggest single cost,* | and it can rise | [YEAR ON YEAR.] Then there's | [GROUND RENT,] | which is smaller, | but check the lease | for any increases | *built in.* There's [MANAGEMENT,] | usually [10 TO 15%] | of the rent | if you use an agent. There's [VOIDS,] | the weeks between tenants | with *no rent* coming in. And then there's | [REPAIRS AND MAINTENANCE,] | which never appear in the advert, | but *always* appear | in your accounts. Here's the [FLAT.] [£250,000,] | with a rent of | [£16,250] a year. That's [6.5%] | in the advert. Take off | a [£2,500] service charge, | [£300] ground rent, | [£1,950] for management | at 12%, | [£1,354] for one month's void. That leaves | [£10,146.] Divided by £250,000, | that's [4.1%,] | and that's before | a *single repair.* A freehold building | works [DIFFERENTLY.] There's no service charge | or ground rent, | but you're responsible | for the *whole building,* | including the *roof* | and the [STRUCTURE.] Here's an *illustrative example:* | a freehold | with a *shop* | and *three flats,* | priced at [£800,000.] With total rent | of [£60,000] a year, | that's [7.5% GROSS.] Take off | [£2,500] | for building insurance, | [£3,000] | for a repairs reserve, | [£6,000] | for management at 10% | and [£3,750] | for one month's void | on the flats. That leaves | [£44,750,] | which is [5.6%.] Both lose money | to [COSTS.] The freehold starts *higher,* | and with no service charge, | less of the rent disappears | before it [REACHES YOU.] Next, | the [TWO TRAPS.] First, | advertised yields are often based | on the [ASKING RENT,] | not the rent | being [PAID.] A flat marketed | at [£1,400] a month | that's actually let | at [£1,250] | has a *lower yield* | than the advert suggests. Always ask | for the *tenancy agreements* | and proof the rent | is being [PAID.] The second | is rents that | [INCLUDE BILLS.] HMO rooms | are often let | with *bills included,* | so the rent figure | looks *higher,* | but the landlord pays | the *council tax,* | *utilities* | and *wifi.* We have a building | for sale in [BROMPTON] | right now, | as an example. It's [9% GROSS] | and [7.8%] | after the bills | the landlord pays | on the rooms. The brochure shows | [BOTH NUMBERS,] | because the second one | is the one | that you *live on.* Before you make an offer, | ask for [THESE.] The *service charge accounts* | for the last three years, | any notices | of *planned major works,* | the *insurance schedule,* | the *tenancy agreements* | and the *rent statements,* | and on a freehold, | a [SURVEY] | that tells you | what the building will need | in the next [FIVE YEARS.] With those in front of you, | you can work out | the net yield [PROPERLY,] | rather than trusting the figure | on the listing. The last part | is [FINANCE.] Net yield | tells you | what the *building* earns. Return on cash | tells you | what *you* earn | on the money you put in. Using the Brompton figures, | with a [30% DEPOSIT] | and interest-only finance | at [6%,] | the income after interest | is [£36,380] a year. That's a | [10.7% RETURN] | on the cash you put in. Those figures are *illustrative* | and set out in the | *investment summary.* Borrowing can increase | the return on your cash, | but only if the net yield | is [HIGHER] | than your borrowing cost. If the net yield | is *below* the interest rate, | the debt [COSTS YOU] | money every month. That's why | you work out the net yield [FIRST,] | then decide | how to finance it. So when you look | at your next listing, | ask for the [COSTS] | before you look | at the yield. Gross yield | gets your *attention.* Net yield | is what tells you | whether to [BUY.] If you found this useful, | send it to someone | who's looking at | their *first investment property.* And if you want to be kept up to date | with new property strategies, | then [SUBSCRIBE.] If you want to be notified | when properties like this | become available, | you can register | at calibreacquire.co.uk/register. I look at every registration | [PERSONALLY,] | and I'll be in touch | if it's a good fit.
